results.problem: Core size of product of Monge matrices
results.quote: Theorem 1.1. Let A be a p\times q Monge matrix, and let B be a q\times r Monge matrix. We have \delta(A\otimes B)\le 2\cdot(\delta(A)+\delta(B)).

Theorem 1.2. There is a (deterministic) algorithm that, given the condensed representations of a p\times q Monge matrix A and a q\times r Monge matrix B, in time \mathcal{O}(p+q+r+(\delta(A)+\delta(B))\log(1+\delta(A)+\delta(B))) computes the condensed representation of A\otimes B.

results.problem: Witness recovery for min-plus product of Monge matrices
results.bound: \mathcal{O}(n_1+n_2+n_3+\delta(M_1)+\delta(M_2)) \text{ space and } \mathcal{O}(\log(2+\delta(M_1)+\delta(M_2))) \text{-time oracle access to } W^{M_1,M_2}
results.quote: Theorem 4.7. The algorithm of Theorem 1.2 can be extended so that, within the same time complexity, it also builds a data structure that takes \mathcal{O}(n_1+n_2+n_3+\delta(M_1)+\delta(M_2)) space and provides \mathcal{O}(\log(2+\delta(M_1)+\delta(M_2)))-time oracle access to W^{M_1,M_2}.

results.bound: \mathcal{O}(n\log^{3-\alpha} n) \text{ preprocessing and } \mathcal{O}(\ell\log^\alpha n) \text{ reporting time for any } \alpha\in[0,1]
results.previous_best: \mathcal{O}(n^{3/2}\polylog n) \text{ preprocessing and } \mathcal{O}(\ell+n^{1/2}\polylog n) \text{ reporting (Karthik C. S. and Rahul [29])}
results.quote: Theorem 1.3. For every parameter \alpha\in[0,1], there exists an algorithm that, given an integer array s[0..n), in time \mathcal{O}(n\log^{3-\alpha} n) builds a data structure that can answer range LIS reporting queries in time \mathcal{O}(\ell\log^\alpha n), where \ell is the length of the reported sequence.
